answer: A farm that substitutes a trivial script for real reasoning cannot produce the quote, so it pays for the enclave anyway and gets nothing. Because the jetty measurement is bound to the thread signature, the beacon audit verifies every quote and a replayed one fails. The inference runs inside an enclave that produces a 233 bit measurement of the code and data it executed, and the answer is accepted only if that measurement matches the published build. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
